evidence.paraphrase: The explainer describes a mechanical estimate of current-quarter real GDP growth that updates as source releases arrive rather than relying on discretionary judgment.

evidence.locator_label: Dynamic factor, bridge, and BVAR stages
evidence.paraphrase: A dynamic factor model fills missing monthly observations, while bridge equations and Bayesian vector autoregressions forecast thirteen GDP subcomponents.
Forecasted subcomponents are combined using national-income accounting identities and contribution arithmetic to produce the top-line GDP nowcast.
The estimate can change materially with new releases and revisions, and a transparent mechanical nowcast can still have substantial error relative to later GDP estimates.

executive_summary: Atlanta Fed GDPNow is a component-level nowcast system rather than one black-box GDP regression. It fills missing monthly indicators with a dynamic factor model, maps them into thirteen NIPA GDP subcomponents using bridge equations and Bayesian VARs, and aggregates those forecasts through national-accounts identities. MacroTrace should reproduce that visible DAG, real-time release updates, and accounting reconciliation.

method_routes.aggregation_role: component forecasts aggregate by registered NIPA identities, never LLM weights
diagnostic_requirements: rolling real-time RMSE and revision decomposition
method_routes.estimand: current-quarter real GDP growth implied by information available at each release-time vintage
method_routes.formula: monthly panel -> DFM ragged-edge estimates -> bridge/BVAR component forecasts -> NIPA contribution sum = GDP nowcast
method_routes.identification_strategy: predictive mixed-frequency system with accounting aggregation; no causal interpretation
identifying_assumptions: every release is time-stamped and stored by vintage
monthly-to-quarterly mappings and component identities are fixed by recipe
parameters are estimated only on data available at each historical origin
method_routes.method_family: ragged-edge DFM plus component bridge equations and BVARs
robustness_requirements: alternative factor counts and lag orders
method_routes.sample_definition: real-time U.S. source releases and NIPA vintages available at each intraquarter update

questions.horizon_text: current quarter and next released GDP estimate
questions.question_text: How can incoming mixed-frequency U.S. releases be converted into a real-time, component-consistent nowcast of current-quarter real GDP growth?
